CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFPARAM

CFPARAM makes sure a variable is defined before the page relies on it. If the variable is missing and you supply a DEFAULT, the default is set; without a DEFAULT, a missing variable stops the page with an error. With TYPE, the value is also checked for the right kind of data.

Category

Variable manipulation

Syntax

<CFPARAM NAME="param_name"
    DEFAULT="value"
    TYPE="data_type">

Attributes

NAME
Required. Name of the variable to check, with a scope prefix if you like (URL.Start, Form.Email, Session.Cart). Dotted names create the structures on the way.
DEFAULT
Optional. Value to give the variable if it does not exist. Without it, a missing variable raises an error, which is how you declare a parameter as required.
TYPE
Optional, default "any". Data type the value must have: any, array, binary, boolean, date, numeric, query, string, struct, UUID (in the 35-character CreateUUID format) or variableName (a legal CFML variable name). A value of the wrong type raises an error.

Usage

CFPARAM is the polite way to read URL and form parameters: put a few at the top of the page and the rest of the template can use URL.Start without wrapping every reference in IsDefined. It does nothing to a variable that already exists, apart from the TYPE check.

Both errors are of type Application, so you can catch them with CFTRY/CFCATCH and show a friendlier message. A wrong type reports "Invalid parameter type."; a missing required parameter reports "Parameter validation error for tag CFPARAM.".

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Defaults for the form fields; the form posts back to this page --->
<CFPARAM NAME="URL.Department" DEFAULT="Engineering">
<CFPARAM NAME="URL.MinSalary" DEFAULT="50000">

<FORM ACTION="cfparam.cfm" METHOD="GET">
Department <INPUT TYPE="Text" NAME="Department" VALUE="<CFOUTPUT>#URL.Department#</CFOUTPUT>" SIZE=12>
earning at least <INPUT TYPE="Text" NAME="MinSalary" VALUE="<CFOUTPUT>#URL.MinSalary#</CFOUTPUT>" SIZE=8>
<INPUT TYPE="Submit" VALUE="Show">
</FORM>

<CFTRY>
  <CFPARAM NAME="URL.MinSalary" TYPE="numeric">
  <CFQUERY NAME="Staff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
  SELECT FirstName, LastName, Salary FROM Employees
  WHERE Department = '#URL.Department#' AND Salary >= #URL.MinSalary#
  ORDER BY Salary DESC
  </CFQUERY>
  <CFOUTPUT><P>#Staff.RecordCount# employee(s) found.</P></CFOUTPUT>
  <UL>
  <CFOUTPUT QUERY="Staff"><LI>#FirstName# #LastName#, #DollarFormat(Salary)#</CFOUTPUT>
  </UL>
<CFCATCH TYPE="Application">
  <CFOUTPUT><P><B>#CFCATCH.Message#</B> #CFCATCH.Detail#</P></CFOUTPUT>
</CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
